author: pk910
content:
I've implemented execution proof indexing & verification in Dora, but everything depends on a way to actually receive the proofs.

If I got the current implementation stage right (at least in Lighthouse),  the `ExecutionProofEnvelope` is basically a gossip-only object. The clients do not intend to store it,  hence there's no GET endpoint to fetch it from a client. The proof is basically passed through and used for the payload verification only.
The POST exists only as the prover's entry point into gossip. And without `--proof-engine-endpoint` a node doesn't even subscribe to the `execution_proof` topic.

That leaves a gap for explorers, that just want to see the proofs in any way.
So, how about adding a `--subscribe-execution-proofs` flag, that makes the client subscribe to the p2p topic and emit the proofs via an event stream topic? That would pass through the proofs without any persistence, and would allow receiving the proofs even without the full verifier setup.

author: manunlp
content:
[Prysm `optional-proofs` branch](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17690) implements the `execution_proof` event.
It carries `SignedExecutionProofEnvelope` JSON.

```
event: execution_proof
data: {"message":{"proof_data":"0x…","proof_type":"2","beacon_block_root":"0x…"},"validator_index":"7","signature":"0x…"}
```

Is this something that would suit Dora needs?

content:
